web_evidence.title: Writing Techniques in The Carpetbaggers
web_evidence.note: This Gale-credited structural guide explicitly states that the novel has nine books: odd-numbered books are narrated in first person by Jonas Cord, while even-numbered books use third-person narration focused on Nevada Smith, Rina Marlowe, David Woolf, and Jennie Denton.

web_evidence.title: The Carpetbaggers Analysis
web_evidence.note: The analysis independently describes the same book-level pattern: first-person Jonas Cord narration in odd-numbered books and third-person narration in even-numbered books.

web_evidence.note: The review says the story moves among five characters' points of view, but it does not distinguish grammatical narrative person and therefore cannot by itself support ALTERNATING.

search_log: Searched "The Carpetbaggers" Harold Robbins excerpt, first chapter, point of view, first person, third person, narrator, and alternating narration.
Opened the BookRags/Gale writing-techniques page and found an explicit whole-book description of the odd-book first-person/even-book third-person structure.
Opened the eNotes analysis and found a second explicit description of the alternating structure, but treated it as Tier C rather than a second strong independent Tier A/B source.
Checked Google Books and Open Library/Internet Archive records; they verified the nine-book edition and preview availability but exposed no usable sustained prose establishing both narrative persons.
Checked the Macmillan publisher page; its synopsis verifies the title but is not narrative-person evidence.
Checked a reader review describing five points of view; because focal viewpoint does not establish grammatical narrative person, it was recorded as supporting none.
person_note: The sampled passages repeatedly expose Jonas Cord's participating first-person narration, including exterior action and speech beats, but they contain no diagnostic passage from the third-person books. Whole-book structural research resolves this sampling limitation: the odd-numbered books use Jonas's first-person narration and the even-numbered books use sustained third-person narration, so the correct book-level label is ALTERNATING. Confidence is med because quote evidence supports only the FIRST component and only one web source is Tier A/B with supports exactly ALTERNATING; the second explicit ALTERNATING source is Tier C, so the required two-source threshold for high confidence is not met.
